title: Disabled and accented SVG variants mutate the shared regular icon
observed: AppIcons.disabled(ADD,16) returns exactly the cached regular icon and replaces its colour filter. A later regular lookup retains that modified filter.
fix: Give regular/disabled/accent variants separate immutable cache entries or copies. Never mutate an icon already handed to another component.
acceptance: Acquire all three variants in each order; existing regular icon retains its original filter. Check enabled/disabled toolbars across theme changes.

title: System-theme timeout does not bound subprocess output reads
observed: SystemTheme.run waits for readLine EOF before the timed waitFor. A silent three-second process completes successfully after 3004ms despite a two-second timeout. Theme's Swing Timer invokes this path on the EDT; an unresponsive desktop command can freeze the UI.
fix: Move desktop discovery off EDT, bound the whole subprocess lifetime including output collection, cap output and cancel/kill timed-out children. Apply only the latest result on EDT.
acceptance: A silent or never-ending test process respects the deadline; typing and repainting remain responsive during the probe. No physical OS-theme hang was reproduced in this audit.

title: Palette rebuilds retain discarded tiles through strong theme listeners
observed: Each ComponentTile registers this::repaint in Theme's static strong listener list. ComponentPalette.rebuild removes tiles and constructs new ones without unregistering; palette and shell callbacks also need lifecycle ownership. Growth follows rebuilds; user-visible slowdown was not measured.
fix: Use paired attach/detach subscriptions with stable listener identity, or a palette-owned theme subscription that repaints current tiles. Dispose project/library listeners too.
acceptance: After repeated filter/pin/theme/window cycles, retained listeners return to the live-component baseline; removed tiles can be collected.

title: Automatic OS-theme changes bypass the canvas palette refresh path
observed: The System Theme timer calls Theme.apply, which changes LaF and fires listeners. AppPreferences.applyThemeColors and refreshProjectsForTheme are only called separately by the preference combo and startup; the automatic path has no equivalent palette update.
fix: Use one ordered theme transaction for startup, preference changes and OS notifications: resolve mode, load theme-specific palette, update UI and editors, repaint all document views, notify listeners on EDT.
acceptance: A simulated OS-theme change updates chrome, canvas, values, diagram, editor and cached previews together; explicit user colours remain preserved. Physical OS-switch path remains to be tested.

title: Generated build ID can identify a previous commit
observed: QA jar and current build jar have identical SHA256, but generated title reports main/2532c84d while repository HEAD is 0a6226664. genBuildInfo inputs omit Git revision/ref, so a commit with unchanged source need not regenerate metadata.
fix: Include resolved Git revision/branch as task input, or another reproducible revision provider. Record commit, dirty status and jar hash in QA manifests independently of UI title.
acceptance: Building after a commit-only change reports the new revision; clean and dirty QA binaries are distinguishable without exposing build noise in the normal title.

title: Recovered QA harness does not fully isolate home or faithfully capture all window sizes
observed: Original qa.sh isolates preferences but not user.home, while unnamed autosaves use user.home. Its shot command hardcodes a 2560x1600 black canvas and composites windows by area rather than stacking order. Old recent lists contain assistant scratch files. Screenshot-edge and first-launch claims need special care.
fix: Isolate home, prefs, documents and autosaves; validate session IDs/PIDs; never recursively reset a broad/unvalidated path; capture actual window geometry and stacking or native compositor output. Archive metadata and unscaled crops. Preserve existing user recents/autosaves.
acceptance: QA leaves user preference and autosave checksums unchanged, refuses unsafe session IDs and stale PIDs, and captures 1280x800 and 2560x1600 without artificial clipping.
